extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: A benchmark and automated multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation, focused on interactive visual artifacts and checklist-guided MLLM-as-Judge scoring.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated through a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. Candidates were aggregated, filtered, de-duplicated, rewritten for clarity/executability, difficulty-calibrated post hoc, and paired with generated/refined checklists.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Automated filters dropped incomplete items; the paper also notes pruning underspecified items and removing tasks solved only by brittle hacks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompt rewriting by experts and LLMs; difficulty assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models; sub-categories tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks; checklist items were LLM-drafted and human-refined.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items; two-stage de-duplication used MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts/checklists/normalized DOM-CSS-JS and screenshot perceptual hashing; flagged items were re-authored or discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed was used as calibration anchors, and human spot-checks were used for sub-category tagging.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The seed checklist achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators. Human validation used a double-blind study with multiple engineers; the final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings. Pair ACC was used to measure agreement between automated and human judgments.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 checklist per query; human validation used multiple annotators, but the paper does not specify a fixed number of labels per dataset item.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience; the paper also mentions front-end engineers and experts, but provides no further demographic details.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos for checklist generation; Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B as MLLM referees; a lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging; MinHash, semantic similarity, and screenshot perceptual hashing for filtering/deduplication.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the benchmark, evaluation harness, baseline results, dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are open-sourced/released. No explicit versioning, update schedule, maintainers, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The query quality filtering prompt explicitly aims to select privacy-free queries and avoid sensitive personal information; no sensitive human attributes are described as collected in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to accelerate development of user-centric generative models and improve evaluation of interactive visual artifacts, with emphasis on real-world user experience and alignment with human preferences.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that human preference may underweight some static code-centric qualities, and that the benchmark is calibrated using aggregated performance of 30+ models. It also discusses potential cognitive biases across different MLLM referees.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark evaluates dynamic behavior using three staged screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture long-horizon or state-dependent interactions. It currently focuses on final artifacts from a single turn and does not assess agentic iterative development. The paper also notes that some tasks are static when visual fidelity or structured graphics are the primary goals.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of LLMs for interactive visual artifact generation; automated scoring; model ranking; diagnostic analysis; human-alignment validation; not presented as a training dataset.
